object_description: long two-storey building over a sunken gymnasium base
design_condition: The new building borders the schoolyard to the north and is sunk into the slope edge, while a separate rooftop kindergarten volume sits on the fire-station building and planted embankments connect the upper and lower play and sports levels.

positive.statement: The landscaped topographical edge creates learning landscapes in partial shade and an arrival point in front of the gymnasium.

position.rationale: The separated lower mass and adjacent open strip visibly suggest the sloping landscape edge.

positive.statement: The zig-zag path guarantees a threshold-free connection between the lower and upper levels.

position.rationale: The diagonal lower element provides the clearest sampled approximation to the connecting path.

positive.statement: The low overall height preserves the dominance of the existing wing from the schoolyard.

position.rationale: The long low main volume and distinct rooftop blocks are visible across the calibrated views.

positive.statement: The sports-floor access and organization are well placed.

position.rationale: Access is not individually visible, so the lower sports-base edge supplies the approximate location.

positive.statement: The careful open-space design ties the two levels together and responds harmoniously to the dimensions of the new building through tree planting.

position.rationale: The visible gap and lower detached form represent the connection between upper and lower outdoor levels.

positive.statement: The implemented upper-floor clusters work well.

position.rationale: Three distinct rooftop or upper-level clusters are clearly visible in the top view and elevations.

negative.statement: The kindergarten playground is likely to create territorial problems because of its proximity to the childcare rooms.

position.rationale: The playground is not sampled, so the upper northern side near the rooftop volume provides a constrained anchor.

negative.statement: The stairs should be more generous for the schoolchildren using the lower level during breaks.

position.rationale: Stairs are not distinguishable; the lower-level connection zone is the useful approximation.

negative.statement: The hidden stair and ramp exits do not correspond to the increased importance of the connection to the playing fields.

position.rationale: Exits are absent as distinct points, so they are placed along the lower connection edge.

negative.statement: The main access from the street has not been upgraded, and the street space along the other street is not convincing.

position.rationale: Street access is not identifiable; the western lower perimeter provides the directional approximation.

negative.statement: The large form appears imposing from the north and west, reinforced by the vertical façade structure and asphalt parking apron.

position.rationale: The long form is most exposed toward the stated north and west sides in the sampled envelope.

negative.statement: The room structure for childcare and services is less convincing, and access requires crossing a room-deep vestibule.

position.rationale: Interior room structure is not visible; the upper building zone provides a plausible anchor.

negative.statement: The façade design is interesting but not very site-specific.

position.rationale: The sampled perimeter shows the façade envelope, though not its site-specific design intent.

negative.statement: The auditorium is too small for the size of the school and does not meet user requirements.

position.rationale: The auditorium is interior and absent, so the lower central building base is used as an approximation.

negative.statement: The spatial program is not completely fulfilled, and the division between new and existing buildings leaves something to be desired.

position.rationale: Program completeness is building-wide; the main sampled volume provides a distributed representative anchor.
